headline: If adopted, this resolution would have overturned a 2019 Education Department rule on how student loan borrowers can seek discharges when a school misrepresented facts.
what_it_does: The resolution would have canceled a September 23, 2019 Department of Education rule that changed how borrowers get a discharge, or cancellation, of federal student loans when a school misrepresented a material fact. The 2019 rule would have required each borrower to apply individually for a borrower defense to repayment. Under the earlier 2016 rule, one application could be filed for an entire group, such as veterans.

who_it_affects.group: Student loan borrowers who say their school misrepresented important facts
who_it_affects.how: They would have kept the option to seek loan discharge without the individual-application requirement in the 2019 rule.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and other groups of borrowers who may have been covered by a single group application
who_it_affects.how: They would have been able to rely on group applications again instead of filing separately under the 2019 rule.

who_it_affects.group: Colleges and other institutions of higher education
who_it_affects.how: They would have faced the accountability standards from the earlier rule rather than those in the 2019 rule.
It would have had to follow the resolution and no longer apply the 2019 rule's process.
